key_insight: TDFold reframes 3D protein structure prediction as a 2D image‑like diffusion task: applying a geometric template diffusion on 2D geometry representations yields more accurate, faster, and more efficient single‑sequence structure predictions.
problem_solved: Reduces reliance on expensive multiple sequence alignments and heavy 3D modeling by enabling accurate, rapid protein structure prediction from a single amino‑acid sequence with lower computational cost.
method: Map 3D geometry to 2D image‑like templates (distance/angle/geometry maps) and perform diffusion denoising in this 2D space.
Use a geometric template diffusion framework to iteratively refine 2D geometry, then reconstruct high‑quality 3D structures from the denoised 2D maps.
Design for single‑sequence input to boost inference speed and efficiency while maintaining or improving accuracy over leading baselines.
impact: Offers ML practitioners a lightweight, scalable diffusion strategy that accelerates structure prediction pipelines and lowers compute barriers for protein design and genomics applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input single sequence → 2D geometry templates → 2D diffusion denoising → 3D reconstruction
Bar chart: accuracy and inference time comparison (TDFold vs MSA‑based and other diffusion/learned-structure baselines)
Before/after visualization: noisy 2D map vs denoised 2D map and resulting 3D structures
Icon set: single-sequence input, speed/efficiency meter, and accuracy trophy
paper_title: Two-dimensional geometric template diffusion for boosting single-sequence protein structure prediction
paper_authors: Xudong Wang, Tong Zhang, Zhen Cui, Xu Guo, Fuyun Wang
